newsitem.title: USA: UPS wins vote on Postal Service growth-WSJ.
newsitem.headline: UPS wins vote on Postal Service growth-WSJ.

text.p: The House Appropriations Committee voted Tuesday to freeze expansion of a unit of the U.S Postal Service that competes overseas with United Parcel Service of America Inc, The Wall Street Journal said.

In Wednesday's electronic edition, the paper said the 29-18 vote testifies to UPS's clout in Congress and reflects a larger battle between UPS and the Postal Service over growing mail-order markets overseas.
The Postal Service has jumped ahead in the competition with its two-year-old Global Postal Link program that helps large shippers move parcels faster through foreign customs, The Journal said.
While now confined to Japan, the United Kingdom and Canada, Global Postal Link expects to expand to Chile, China, Germany and Mexico in the near future, the paper said.
But the vote calls for a one-year freeze on expansion until Congress can review the situation, the paper said.
UPS had lobbied for the freeze, saying the rival's government status gives it unfair advantage in dealing with foreign customs agencies.
